# package client

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-ethernetip/client"
```

Package client is an EtherNet/IP originator of explicit messages.

A [Client](#type-client) holds one TCP connection and encapsulation session with a target. It sends unconnected requests with SendRRData, routed through the target's Connection Manager with Unconnected\_Send when a route is set ([WithRoute](#func-withroute)), and opens connected (Class 3) messaging connections with Forward\_Open ([Client.OpenConnection](#func-client-openconnection)), whose requests travel in SendUnitData. [Client.ForwardOpen](#func-client-forwardopen) and [Client.ForwardClose](#func-client-forwardclose) are also the building blocks of the scanner package's I/O connections.

[Discover](#func-discover) and [ListIdentity](#func-listidentity) find devices with ListIdentity over UDP.

Every call takes a context.Context; a request's wait ends at the earlier of the context's deadline and the client's timeout ([WithTimeout](#func-withtimeout)). Errors match the sentinels of the root package with errors.Is (ErrTimeout, ErrConnectionLost, ErrNotConnected, ...) and carry the target's answer as \*ethernetip.CIPError or \*ethernetip.EncapError.

## Constants

```go
const DefaultVendorID uint16 = 0xFFFF
```

DefaultVendorID is the originator vendor ID the client puts in Forward\_Open requests unless WithOriginator sets another. No ODVA vendor ID is assigned to this library: 0xFFFF marks the originator as unregistered. Products should use their own vendor ID.

### type Client

```go
type Client struct {

	// turn admits WithMaxPending unconnected requests at a time.

	// connMu serialises Connect, so that two requests reconnecting at once
	// dial once.

}
```

Client is an EtherNet/IP originator of explicit messages: one TCP connection and one encapsulation session with a target. Create it with [New](#func-new) or [Dial](#func-dial).

A Client is safe for concurrent use. Unconnected requests of several goroutines are sent one after the other, or up to WithMaxPending at a time, and their replies are matched by sender context. Connected requests of a [Conn](#type-conn) are matched by connection ID and sequence count.

#### func New

```go
func New(addr string, opts ...Option) (*Client, error)
```

New returns a client for the target at addr ("host:port"; the port defaults to 44818, or 2221 with WithTLS). The client is not connected until Connect.

Addr returns the address of the target.

#### func (Client) Close

```go
func (c *Client) Close() error
```

Close unregisters the session and closes the connection. Pending requests fail with ErrClosed. Close first waits for a write in progress, which ends within the client's timeout (WithTimeout). Close is idempotent.

#### func (Client) Connect

```go
func (c *Client) Connect(ctx context.Context) error
```

Connect dials the target and registers a session. It does nothing when the client is connected. It fails with an error that matches ErrConnectFailed and wraps the cause.

#### func (Client) Do

```go
func (c *Client) Do(ctx context.Context, req cip.Request) (cip.Response, error)
```

Do sends an unconnected explicit request (SendRRData), through Unconnected\_Send when the client has a route, and returns the response.

A response whose general status is not success is returned together with a \*ethernetip.CIPError, so that its data (some services return data with an error, and partial transfers carry a fragment) is not lost.

#### func (Client) DoRoute

```go
func (c *Client) DoRoute(ctx context.Context, req cip.Request, route cip.Path) (cip.Response, error)
```

DoRoute is Do with route in place of the client's route: nil sends the request to the target itself.

#### func (Client) ForwardClose

```go
func (c *Client) ForwardClose(ctx context.Context, fc cip.ForwardClose) error
```

ForwardClose closes a connection with Forward\_Close. The client's route, if any, is prefixed to the connection path.

#### func (Client) ForwardOpen

```go
func (c *Client) ForwardOpen(ctx context.Context, fo cip.ForwardOpen, items ...encap.Item) (cip.ForwardOpenReply, []encap.Item, error)
```

ForwardOpen sends a Forward\_Open (or, with fo.Large, a Large\_Forward\_Open) to the target's Connection Manager. The client's route, if any, is prefixed to the connection path. items are added to the request's common packet format (a Sockaddr Info T->O item tells the target where to send I/O data); the reply's other items (Sockaddr Info) are returned with the reply.

A refusal is a \*ethernetip.CIPError with general status 0x01 and the Connection Manager's extended status (cip.ConnectionStatus).

#### func (Client) GetAttributeList

```go
func (c *Client) GetAttributeList(ctx context.Context, class cip.Class, instance uint32, ids []uint16, sizes []int) ([]AttributeValue, error)
```

GetAttributeList reads several attributes with service 0x03. sizes gives the encoded size of each attribute's value, which the reply does not carry; a size of 0 takes the rest of the reply (the last attribute only). The reply's status may be 0x0A (attribute list error) with values for the attributes that were read: the result is returned together with the error.

#### func (Client) MultipleService

```go
func (c *Client) MultipleService(ctx context.Context, reqs []cip.Request) ([]cip.Response, error)
```

MultipleService sends reqs in one Multiple Service Packet (0x0A) to the Message Router and returns one response per request, in order. The packet's own status 0x1E (embedded service error) is not an error: each response carries its status; use [ResponseError](#func-responseerror) to turn one into an error.

### type Conn

```go
type Conn struct {

	// one request at a time

}
```

Conn is a connected (Class 3) explicit messaging connection. Requests are sent with SendUnitData, one at a time, in the order they are made. A Conn is safe for concurrent use. It ends with Close, when the session is lost, or when the target times it out for inactivity.

#### func (Conn) Close

```go
func (cn *Conn) Close(ctx context.Context) error
```

Close closes the connection with Forward\_Close. A request in flight fails with ErrClosed. The connection is unusable afterwards even when Forward\_Close fails (the target then times it out). Close is idempotent.

### type ConnectionOptions

```go
type ConnectionOptions struct {
	// Timeout is how long the target keeps the connection without a
	// request: it times out after RPI × 4 << multiplier, which the client
	// derives from it. Zero means 60 seconds.
	Timeout time.Duration
	// Size is the connection size in octets, the largest request and
	// reply. Zero means 500, or 4000 with Large.
	Size uint16
	// Large opens the connection with Large_Forward_Open, for sizes above
	// 511 octets.
	Large bool
	// Path is the application path of the connection; nil means the
	// Message Router (@2/1).
	Path cip.Path
}
```

ConnectionOptions configures a connected (Class 3) explicit messaging connection.

#### func Discover

```go
func Discover(ctx context.Context, opts DiscoverOptions) ([]Device, error)
```

Discover sends one ListIdentity request over UDP and returns the devices that answered, in the order of their replies, each address once. It sends exactly one datagram: it does not scan.

#### func ListIdentity

```go
func ListIdentity(ctx context.Context, addr string) (Device, error)
```

ListIdentity asks one device for its identity over UDP and returns the first reply. addr is the device's address; the port defaults to 44818.

### type DiscoverOptions

```go
type DiscoverOptions struct {
	// Address is where the ListIdentity request is sent: a broadcast
	// address ("255.255.255.255", "192.168.1.255") or a single device. The
	// port defaults to 44818. Required.
	Address string
	// Local is the local address to send from (and so the interface);
	// empty picks any.
	Local string
	// Wait is how long replies are collected. Devices delay their reply to
	// a broadcast by up to MaxDelay. Zero means 2 seconds; the context's
	// deadline, when earlier, ends it.
	Wait time.Duration
	// MaxDelay is the largest delay a device may add to its reply, which
	// the request carries in its sender context (milliseconds). Zero
	// leaves it to the device's default (2 seconds by the specification).
	MaxDelay time.Duration
	// MaxDevices stops collecting after that many replies; zero means
	// 1024.
	MaxDevices int
}
```

DiscoverOptions configures [Discover](#func-discover).

### type Doer

```go
type Doer interface {
	Do(ctx context.Context, req cip.Request) (cip.Response, error)
}
```

Doer sends an explicit request and returns the response. \*[Client](#type-client) (unconnected messaging) and \*[Conn](#type-conn) (connected messaging) implement it, so that code such as the logix package works over either.

### type Option

```go
type Option func(*options) error
```

Option configures a [Client](#type-client).

#### func WithAutoReconnect

```go
func WithAutoReconnect() Option
```

WithAutoReconnect makes a request on a client whose session was lost reconnect first, instead of failing with ErrNotConnected. Connected (Class 3) connections are not reopened: they end with the session.

#### func WithDialer

```go
func WithDialer(d Dialer) Option
```

WithDialer sets the dialer of the TCP connection.

#### func WithLogger

```go
func WithLogger(l ethernetip.Logger) Option
```

WithLogger sets the logger. Logging is silent by default.

#### func WithMaxPacket

```go
func WithMaxPacket(n int) Option
```

WithMaxPacket sets the largest encapsulation data length the client accepts from the target; a larger packet closes the session. Default and maximum 65535.

#### func WithMaxPending

```go
func WithMaxPending(n int) Option
```

WithMaxPending sets how many unconnected requests may be outstanding on the session at once. Further requests wait for their turn. The default, 1, suits every target; targets that process requests concurrently answer faster with more.

#### func WithMetrics

```go
func WithMetrics(m ethernetip.Metrics) Option
```

WithMetrics sets the metrics callbacks; a value that also implements [ethernetip.RequestMetrics](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-ethernetip#RequestMetrics) receives every request.

#### func WithOriginator

```go
func WithOriginator(vendorID uint16, serial uint32) Option
```

WithOriginator sets the originator vendor ID and serial number that identify the client's connections (the connection triad of Forward\_Open). By default the vendor ID is DefaultVendorID and the serial number is random.

#### func WithRoute

```go
func WithRoute(route cip.Path) Option
```

WithRoute routes every unconnected request through the target's Connection Manager with Unconnected\_Send along route, and prefixes the connection path of every Forward\_Open with it: for example cip.ParseRoute("1/0") reaches the controller in slot 0 of a ControlLogix chassis through its EtherNet/IP module.

#### func WithStateHandler

```go
func WithStateHandler(f func(ethernetip.State, error)) Option
```

WithStateHandler sets a function called when the session's state changes, with the error that caused a disconnection. It is called from the client's goroutines and must not block or call the client.

#### func WithTLS

```go
func WithTLS(cfg *tls.Config) Option
```

WithTLS runs the session over TLS: EtherNet/IP over TLS as CIP Security defines the transport (port 2221 by default). The certificate is verified against ServerName or, when it is empty, the host dialed (as tls.Dial does), with RootCAs or the system's roots.

#### func WithTimeout

```go
func WithTimeout(d time.Duration) Option
```

WithTimeout sets the time a request may take when its context has no earlier deadline: the wait for the reply, and for Connect the dial and RegisterSession. Default 5 seconds.
